threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you're new when you still think the 'Overground' means a paved path, not a whole different layer of transport chaos.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded us with an old Elvis tune, while a cat sat on the aisle—perfectly unbothered.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a toddler bargaining over ice cream with the Kiosk owner while the father just laughed. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings, complete with artisanal vegan food stalls and retro arcade games.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're from SF if they instinctively dodge the guy selling roses by the BART station without breaking stride.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the Muni platform with a ukulele while waiting for the N. Took me back to simpler days—nothing like live music amidst the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think the squares are just for pictures, but locals actually use them for gatherings, games, and late-night chats. It's our heartbeat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they try to order a cortado and end up with a sweetened café con leche instead.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their shock at how long the bus takes, even when it’s just a couple of stops. We all know it’s part of the charm.
Heard a guy on the 35 last night arguing with his phone over who got more plays on Spotify. The whole bus just stared, half amused, half confused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the sound of kids playing in the street perfectly mingled with the aroma of Döner from the corner shop on a warm evening.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when you see a spontaneous dance party break out in the middle of the street during U-Bahn strikes. It's wild!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their tolerance for the Muni delays; they’ve got a backup plan for when there's a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo trying to catch the 5 while balancing a pet iguana. Only in San Francisco do fashion and reptiles collide on the Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a 'tapeo' and sit anywhere. In Gràcia, you’ll get side-eye if you linger too long in a busy bar.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by how often they struggle with the metro card machine; the locals know to avoid those at rush hour.
